description: Map who a company sells to and buys from, with evidence from filings, counterparties' own releases, contracts and import records. Supply-chain alpha.
suggested_questions: Map the key customers and suppliers of Credo Technology (CRDO, credosemi.com): up to 25 relationships, each with evidence.
Map the key customers and suppliers of Vertiv (VRT, vertiv.com): up to 25 relationships, each with evidence.
Map the key customers and suppliers of Celsius Holdings (CELH, celsius.com): up to 25 relationships, each with evidence.
skill:
Where relationships are disclosed:
- The company's own filings: 10-K customer-concentration notes (customers over 10% of revenue, sometimes unnamed as
  "Customer A"), the business section, risk factors naming suppliers, material contracts filed as exhibits (10.x),
  segment notes.
- Counterparties' filings: a customer's 10-K naming the company as a sole or key supplier; a supplier's 10-K naming
  the company as a major customer. Matching an unnamed "Customer A" to a name needs a second source that ties them.
- Company and counterparty releases: supply agreements, design wins, partnership and distribution announcements,
  customer case studies and logo pages, investor presentations.
- Government and trade records: USAspending awards (the government as customer), US import bill-of-lading records
  (public aggregators such as ImportYeti) showing shipper and consignee, FCC filings naming manufacturers.
- Trade press and teardown reports naming component suppliers.

What terms mean:
- relationship: customer, supplier, contract_manufacturer, distributor, partner, licensor, licensee.
- revenue_share_pct is only the percentage a filing prints. It is never estimated.
- status: active (evidence within the last two years), ended (a source says it ended), announced (agreed, not yet
  shipping), cannot_verify.

Where the alpha is: a concentration that the market treats as diversified, a supplier that is the sole source for a
critical part, or a customer relationship that ended without an announcement.

Pitfalls: a logo on a website can be years old; a partnership announcement is not revenue; a subsidiary or a
distributor is not the end customer unless a source says so.

Citations and evidence:
- source_url is one full public https URL: the exact page the value was read on. Never a search results page, an index
  page, an internal file path or a source id. A value from two pages is two values.
- Dates are the date the event happened or the source printed, as YYYY-MM-DD, not today's date.
- Public pages only. Paywalled, logged-in or leaked material, expert-network transcripts and anything marked
  confidential carry MNPI risk and are out of bounds. When only a paywalled article's headline and first lines are
  public, those lines can be used, marked "Headline only:".
- Evidence grades: primary_record (regulator, court, filing, government database, lender schedule, or the live or
  archived page being measured), company_statement, original_press, repeated_press, third_party_tracker. When a page
  repeats a filing, a release or another outlet, the original is the better citation.
- A value nobody published is null. Not an estimate from memory. Analyst opinions, estimates, price targets and
  ratings are views, not evidence.
- Entity drift is the most common error: a namesake, a parent, a subsidiary, a lender or a sister company. Match on
  legal name, ticker, SEC CIK or domain before using a page.

output_schema.description: One row per customer, supplier or partner relationship.

items.description: One row per customer, supplier or partner relationship.

counterparty.description: Name of the customer, supplier or partner.

counterparty_ticker.description: Ticker of the counterparty if listed.

revenue_share_pct.description: Share of the company's revenue as printed in a filing, as a plain number. Null if not printed.

evidence_type.description: Kind of source establishing the relationship.

source_url.description: Full public https URL of the exact page that states this row. Never a search results page, an index page or an internal source id.
